findings.violated_invariant: A deployed commit must not select any executable website.deploy generation path; checks inside event-selected YAML are not a security boundary.
findings.minimal_counterexample: Direct action literals in common runtime or configuration formats such as .vue and .properties remained outside the previous declared extension set, while a substring matcher rejected the unrelated literal notwebsite.deployment.
counterexample_history: A manually supplied deployment identifier or redirecting lookalike URL could pass an existence probe while a CI-local build digest was described as deployed-output identity.
The deployed-commit caller passed GLYPH_DEPLOY_KEY and contents:write into event-controlled code, while a direct-HTTP-200 requirement overstated an SSO-protected URL-to-bytes relationship.
A digest-only candidate still executed verifier and minter code selected by the deployed commit.
Deleting the known workflow and script filenames did not prove that an alternate executable name or YAML spelling could not recreate the same path.

A workflow using on: [deployment_status] invoked an alternate glyph/scripts/site-proof.mjs. The first recursive guard neither recognized the flow-form trigger nor recursively inspected the indirectly invoked executable.

A root package command invoked packages/neutral.mjs, or a workflow invoked an .mts or composite-action implementation. These paths sat outside the next scanner scope and could reconstruct website.deploy generation.

Direct literals and ordinary builders under bulla/tools, glyph/data, a source directory named coverage, public TOML, and benchmark Cargo metadata exposed further allowlist gaps; split workflow fields and quoted publication authority exposed a correlation gap.
findings.affected_claim: No website.deploy candidate, deployment binding, or verification rung is produced by repository automation.
findings.correction: Retained the blocked capability state and narrowed the mechanized claim after repeated lexical-completeness failures. The guard enumerates tracked files with git, applies strict UTF-8 and size checks, scans declared common runtime and configuration formats, recursively scans the two repository script roots, parses package commands, and analyzes workflow and composite-action YAML. It rejects exact bounded action literals, common escape forms, direct action fields, ordinary join/concatenation and split workflow fields, named or ordinary signing-key constructions, literal local taint paths, and correlated publication authority. The behavioral ledger includes hostile and clean controls for the reviewed cases. The generated status still reports generation, public release, and attestation as BLOCKED_UNIMPLEMENTED and deployed-output binding as NOT_COMPUTED.
residual_limitations: Unrecognized formats, same-file or cross-file dynamic construction outside the enumerated patterns, encoded or indirect construction, and excluded or external artifacts remain review-bound; the gate does not establish lexical completeness or absolute prevention.

Conservative matches remain for some preview subtypes, equality-then-throw deny logic, configuration denylists, and documentation URLs. These are precision debt rather than evidence of a generation path.

The strongest established repository facts are that the removed generation and publication automation is absent, the blocked status fields are exact, and no candidate, public release, attestation, or deployed-output binding is produced by the current tracked tree.
findings.reviewer: Archimedes and Popper role-separated read-only passes found no in-scope ordinary bypass and approved closure under the recorded narrowed static scope

findings.violated_invariant: Workflow no-clobber behavior must not be presented as absolute host immutability or retention, and event-controlled code must not hold release-publication authority.
findings.minimal_counterexample: Aliased split action fields combined with quoted contents:write authority, or a release action whose producer lived outside the previous source roots, could evade the prior same-file publication correlation.
counterexample_history: A commit-derived release asset was uploaded with --clobber, allowing later workflow runs to overwrite publication history.
Content-addressed, no-clobber behavior by one workflow could not establish host retention because the release remained isImmutable:false and administrator-controlled.
The first blocked-state gate did not recursively correlate workflow invocation with alternate publication scripts.
An indirectly invoked alternate executable could reconstruct website.deploy release publication while the first recursive guard checked an incomplete extension and directory set.
A package source with a non-legacy extension or a composite action could execute website.deploy release creation while the next recursive guard did not scan that publication surface.
findings.affected_claim: No public deployment-receipt publication, external retention, or host immutability is established by this sprint.
findings.correction: Within the declared tracked formats and patterns, the scanner rejects direct or ordinary website.deploy construction and correlates tainted sources or action roots with contents:write, secrets, GitHub release actions or commands, and clobber markers. Unrelated release workflows remain accepted because publication authority alone does not establish a website.deploy path. The gate does not establish host immutability, host retention, or completeness beyond its declared static boundary.
residual_limitations: Unrecognized formats and dynamic, encoded, indirect, excluded, or external publication producers remain review-bound.
No host immutability or retention property is inferred from repository workflow absence.
findings.reviewer: Archimedes and Popper role-separated read-only passes approved closure under the narrowed publication correlation and explicit no-immutability boundary

findings.violated_invariant: An event-selected path must not mint either a signed or unsigned artifact that could be mistaken for trusted deployment evidence.

Making the key optional still exposed it to code selected by the deployed commit whenever the key existed.
A digest-only candidate removed the signing secret but still executed attacker-selectable minter and verifier code from the deployed commit.
findings.affected_claim: No integrity or authenticity rung is claimed for website.deploy because no candidate is generated.
findings.correction: Within the declared tracked formats and patterns, the scanner and hostile fixtures reject exact or ordinary split-token website.deploy construction, named and ordinary Glyph deployment key references, signing operations, package indirection, and composite-action invocation. The absence of a generated candidate means no integrity or authenticity rung is claimed.

findings.violated_invariant: A withdrawn public evidence claim must be marked withdrawn at its original discovery surfaces while the original bytes remain available for audit.
findings.minimal_counterexample: GitHub still exposed 52 glyph-deploy releases whose titles and bodies described immutable deployment receipts. The latest retained asset described a local build digest as deployed-output identity and still verified to the digest rung, with no withdrawal pointer at the release entry point.
findings.affected_claim: A reader entering through any repository-operated legacy deployment-receipt release can discover the withdrawal before treating the retained artifact as current deployment evidence.
findings.correction: Published glyph.withdrawn-deployment-receipts/1 with all 52 observed release IDs, tags, original mutable-metadata hashes, asset names, byte lengths, and GitHub-provided SHA-256 digests. Annotated every exact release title and body as WITHDRAWN with immutable links to the falsification record and registry. A guarded reconciliation verified each original metadata hash before mutation and verified all recorded assets unchanged afterward. The public status page links the registry and the complete Glyph check validates its closed schema and inventory.
residual_limitations: The retained receipt bytes necessarily preserve their historical internal wording. A detached copy viewed without its release metadata or the withdrawal registry does not carry an embedded tombstone.
GitHub release titles and bodies remain mutable host metadata. The committed registry preserves their original hashes and asset identities but does not make future host metadata immutable.
The offline registry gate validates the committed inventory. The 2026-07-27 remote reconciliation was an operator action and is not evidence of independent review or permanent host retention.

findings.minimal_counterexample: Unauthenticated requests to the linked immutable FALSIFICATIONS commit and every tombstoned release returned 404 because jkomkov/res-agentica is private. The status page called the inaccessible GitHub target a public withdrawal record.

findings.minimal_counterexample: The worktree-tamper regression created an unreferenced synthetic commit, cloned the shallow CI repository with --shared, and then tried to check out that unreferenced object in the child clone. findings.correction: Remove all secondary checkout and worktree setup. Preserve the exact bytes of one reviewed source in the existing checkout, append the hostile modification, run the real predeployment gate, and restore the exact original bytes in a finally block. Pytest runs these files serially in every declared CI job.
